title: HuginnMindRequest
description:
Every operation a mind answers. `Admit` carries the batch whole because the
batch already names the instance and the asker; a second `instance` beside
it would be two declarations. Every read names the instance because ruling
14 refuses another mind's identity whatever the transport, and a read of
the wrong mind is that same collision on the read side. `Whoami` names
none: it is how a client learns which mind it reached.

oneOf.description: The mind's persona document, if one is stored.

Replaces the mind's persona document whole. `expected_updated_at` is
the stored document's `updatedAt`, none for the first put. The
provenance is the asker's, as for `Admit`.

Faculty.description:
Which faculty a batch was admitted as. Attribution, not authority
(ruling 18): no admission rule trusts it, and Cut 9's views read it back
from the receipt.

ForeignRef.description: A citation of a document in another repo's pipeline store (D6).

FullSha.description: A full git commit id: exactly 40 lowercase hex characters.

LandedName.description: A name the cut landed, and where it lives.

Line.description: Text of at most 1,000 UTF-8 bytes.

MutationRecord.description:
One mutation a report ran: a key-safe label a verdict claim can name,
the exact edit, and the tree it was applied to.

OrgRepo.description:
A GitHub repository as `Org/Repo`, at most 140 UTF-8 bytes (39 + 1 +
100). The owner is 1 to 39 `[A-Za-z0-9-]` bytes with no leading or
trailing hyphen; the repo is 1 to 100 `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` bytes, is never
`.` or `..`, and does not end in `.git`, ASCII-case-insensitively.
Identity is case-insensitive: `GameCult/Epiphany` and `gamecult/epiphany`
are the same repository.

Para.description: Text of at most 4,000 UTF-8 bytes; longer narrative is cited by `DocRef`.

PipelineAdmissionBatch.description:
One admission request: the mind it is for, who asks, and the documents.
Rides the wire whole (`wire::HuginnMindRequest::Admit`).

PipelineDocument.description:
The envelope enum, adjacently tagged on the kind name: a document
on a wire is `{ kind, value }`, and `kind` is exactly what
`PipelineKind::name()` returns, so a reader dispatches on the kind
segment it already knows from the key and needs no second registry
mapping variant spellings to kinds. Adjacent rather than internal
because a value is a named map of its own and an internal tag would
have to be merged into it; the tag stays beside the value instead.
This is not a published schema: `schemas/cultnet` publishes the
fifteen per-kind value documents, and the envelope is the wire's
shape, not a document's.

PipelineHandOff.description:
A reassignment of stewardship, recorded in both minds. `documents` names
what travels with it.

PipelineInstance.description:
A mind's identity document. A store is canonical to exactly one
instance, and this says which; identity lives in the state, not in a
path.

PipelineProvenance.description:
Who admitted a batch: the faculty, the agent, its session and the tool.
A field on the receipt and nothing else; the digest excludes it.

PipelinePulse.description:
One Mind's heartbeat vote, in her own mind: the beat she wants (the swarm's
tempo is the lower median of every Mind's newest vote) and the urgency she
declares for herself until her next Persona turn. Either may be absent, not
both. Instance-rooted: the key is `<instance>:pulse:<label>`, the label
time-ordered like a run's.

PipelineRef.description:
A reference to another document. The id is parsed as a full pipeline id of
the declared `kind`, so the kind and the id's kind segment cannot disagree.

PipelineResolution.description:
The record of how a subject was closed and by what. `sequence` is per
subject and set by the writer, `1` for the first, and it is the last
part of the key, so a subject's resolutions share a prefix and a
withdrawn one is kept under its subject rather than overwritten.
Whether a sequence is the previous plus one, and whether an earlier
resolution still stands, are admission's rules: this crate refuses
neither `0` nor a gap, exactly as it refuses neither `revision: 0` nor
a `revision` with no predecessor.

PipelineRun.description:
One launch of a Self or a Persona turn: the one record of what it took
on. `claims` are the work it holds, and a claim is live while its run
has no resolution in force. `budget_usd` is a canonical decimal string,
`0` for an interactive run. Instance-rooted like stewardship: the key
is `<instance>:run:<label>`. Whether a claim is free is admission's rule.

PipelineStewardship.description:
Stewardship over a repo, as an assignment recorded in a mind. One
instance may steward several repos, so the repo is part of the key.
`sequence` is per `(instance, repo)`, set by the writer, `1` for the
first, so a repo transferred away and back is two records under one
prefix rather than one document overwriting the other. `assigned_on`
is a field, not a key part. As on a resolution, whether the sequence
is the previous plus one, and which assignment is in force, are
admission's rules and not this crate's.

PipelineTarget.description:
`repos`, when non-empty, is the campaign's whole repo set from this
revision on; empty keeps the previous set (ruling campaign-repo-set-home).

Promise.description:
A promise a report makes about what it landed. Not a document and not
resolvable: it is identified by its report's id and its label, as a
`TargetInvariant` is by its target's. Soul measures every one (ruling
A), and the rule that every one is measured is admission's.

ReadAnchor.description: Code Hands must see but not change, in the spec's repo at the spec's base.

ResolutionOutcome.description:
How a subject was resolved. Every referent is a parsed `PipelineRef`, so a
resolution names its records by ids of the kinds they declare, validated
where every other referent is; a `Fixed` commit is a `Sha` whose referent
is outside the document set (ruling B). Whether a named document exists,
and how many may supersede one subject, are admission's rules.

oneOf.description:
Overturned, in whole or in part, by later records. The list is bounded
here because the enum is outside `value_types!`, the only place a list
maximum is emitted automatically.

SemanticQuery.description:
A semantic query: the text to find documents near, and how many. The index
owns which fields of each kind are text (`index_text`), so no substring
filter lives here to become a second answer to that question. `top_k` is
the most rows answered, all of them members of the selection: the
selection decides membership before the index is asked.

Sha.description: A git commit id: 7-40 lowercase hex characters.

Sha256Hex.description: A SHA-256 digest: exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.

Short.description: Text of at most 200 UTF-8 bytes.

Slug.description: A campaign slug or key segment: label parts joined by `.`.

Symbol.description:
A name the location's lines must contain as written there (an
identifier or a YAML `&fileID`); not an identity. 1 to 128 bytes, no
whitespace and no control character.

Title.description:
A title: 1 to 200 UTF-8 bytes, enforced by admission; JSON Schema
length counts characters. Holds at least one alphanumeric character,
no control character, and no bidi control character (`U+061C`,
`U+200E`, `U+200F`, `U+202A`-`U+202E`, `U+2066`-`U+2069`).

VerdictClaim.description:
The promise this claim measured, and the report's mutations it ran. An
`Unproven` claim with a promise is one Soul could not reach.
